title: Initiative supply-chain: map owner-level deliverables to company OKRs and release windows
creator: Aaditya Shah
description:
Background: As Redwood scales cross-functional initiatives, we lack a consistent, machine-readable mapping from team-level deliverables (features, infra work, experiments) to company OKRs and release windows. This gap causes routing friction during quarterly planning, obscures true capacity for OKR delivery, and hides domino risks when one team's delay affects multiple company objectives.

Goal: Create an "initiative supply-chain" framework and a lightweight mapping artifact that: 1) ties each initiative/epic to one or more company-level OKRs with explicit contribution type (lead, contributor, enabler); 2) records release window(s) and critical path deliverables; 3) surfaces cross-team dependencies and single points of failure; 4) integrates with existing roadmap tooling and the Console release registry.

Scope and out-of-scope: In-scope: PM-owned initiatives across Platform, Runtime, Console, and Growth for Q1–Q3 2026; a canonical mapping spreadsheet + JSON export; a visualization for the leadership roadmap sync; a short-run governance checklist for changes. Out-of-scope: full automation across all teams in first pass, rewriting existing ticket hierarchies, or enforcing resource allocation — those are follow-ups.

Approach: 1) Prototype a canonical mapping schema (CSV + small JSON) with fields: initiative_key, initiative_title, owner_team, primary_OKR, contribution_type, planned_release_window, critical_deliverables (list), dependencies (list of keys), estimated_risk (low|med|high), and signals (metrics to track). 2) Run a 3-week pilot with 4 cross-functional initiatives (Serving runtime batching, Dedicated autoscale policy, Console rollouts UX, Private deployment onboarding) to validate content, governance flow, and visualization. 3) Iterate and ship a lightweight template and an integration guide for PMs and Eng leads.

Success metrics: - 90% of pilot initiatives have completed mapping with owner sign-off within the sprint. - Leadership can produce a cross-initiative dependency graph for the roadmap sync with <2 business days of effort. - Reduction in surprise cross-team blocker incidents tied to mapped dependencies by 30% in the following quarter.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: PMs view mapping as additional overhead. Mitigation: keep template minimal, provide a facilitator (Solutions PM) and a 60-minute mapping workshop. - Risk: stale data. Mitigation: tie mapping updates to the release gating checklist and make small JSON export consumable by Console. - Risk: unclear contribution semantics. Mitigation: adopt three contribution types (lead, contributor, enabler) and require owner sign-off.

Stakeholders: Lina Martinez (owner), Eng leads: Marco Chen, Priya Nambiar, Tomas Varela; Design lead: Sera Kim; Head of Product: Maia Thompson; Solutions PM: Arman Reddy.

Artifacts and links: Confluence draft (design + template) -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/space/PM/initiative-supply-chain-prototype; Draft spreadsheet -> Drive link (internal); Roadmap visualization proof-of-concept -> https://short.link/redwood-initiative-graph (prototype).

Deliverables: - Canonical mapping template (CSV + JSON schema) - Pilot mappings for 4 initiatives - One-pager governance + update cadence - Visualization for leadership sync - Integration guide for Console release registry

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.

Next steps (current sprint): 1) Finalize minimal schema (owners: Lina + Marco) 2) Schedule mapping workshops with pilot initiative teams 3) Build CSV -> JSON exporter and upload hook for Console release registry 4) Prepare leadership demo for March 25 roadmap sync.
